settings.name_in_paper: High-dimensional kernelized contextual bandit (inner-product class of kernels)
unmapped: Each arm i has its own context X^(i)(t) in R^d, i.i.d. over rounds (arms' contexts may be correlated), and its own reward function f^(i) in an RKHS with ||f^(i)||_H <= B
Kernel from the inner-product class K(x,x')=h(<x,x'>/d) with h in C^3, h(0)>0, h'(0)>0, h'' bounded below; scaled by 1/d
Whitened contexts have independent bounded coordinates with zero mean and unit variance; ||Sigma|| op <= 1
Noise only assumed to have bounded variance sigma^2 (finite second moment)
High-dimensional regime: d grows polynomially with T
Lenient-regret tuning of T0 uses the lenient tolerance Delta, the covariance parameter epsilon and kernel derivatives h''_min, beta
settings.definition_quote: This paper considers a nonparametric contextual bandit problem with $K$ arms. We consider the fully stochastic setting, where the contexts, as well as the rewards, are drawn from fixed distributions. ... $\Yt = f_\ast^{(I(t))}( \Xt) + \xi(t)$ ... The independent noise term $\xi(t)$ has zero mean and bounded variance $\Var[\xi(t)] \leq \sigma^2$.

settings.name_in_paper: High-dimensional kernelized contextual bandit (RBF class of kernels)
unmapped: Each arm i has its own context X^(i)(t) in R^d, i.i.d. over rounds, and its own reward function f^(i) in an RKHS with ||f^(i)||_H <= B
Kernel from the RBF class K(x,x')=h(||x-x'||^2/d) with h in C^3, h>0, h'<0 on [0,2], h' increasing (includes Gaussian, Laplace, Matern with length scale growing with d)
Whitened contexts have independent bounded coordinates; ||Sigma||_op <= 1
Noise only assumed to have bounded variance sigma^2
High-dimensional regime: d grows polynomially with T
Lenient-regret tuning of T0 uses the lenient tolerance Delta, epsilon, h'_min and c_underline
settings.definition_quote: This paper considers a nonparametric contextual bandit problem with $K$ arms. ... \textbf{Radial-basis function (RBF) Class}: With $h \in C^3$ satisfies $h(x) > 0, h'(x) < 0, \forall x \in [0, 2]$, and $h'(\cdot)$ is monotonically increasing, the class of kernels is defined as $K(x,x') = h(\|x-x'\|^2/d)$.

symbols.tau_1: exponent with d = Theta(T^tau_1), tau_1 in (0,1)
symbols.tau_2: exponent with epsilon = Theta(T^-tau_2), tau_2 in (0, tau_1/4)

conditions: Assumption 4.1 (RKHS norm <= B, ||Sigma||_op <= 1, whitened contexts with independent bounded coordinates)
low-rank covariance Sigma = diag(1,...,1,0,...,0) with rank epsilon d (Case I), epsilon = Theta(T^-tau_2), tau_2 in (0, tau_1/4)

source.label: thm:etc_reg_simple
source.quote: Consider a kernel from the inner-product class as Definition \ref{def:kernel_class}. Suppose that $d = \Theta(T^{\tau_1})$ and Assumption~\ref{asmp:basic} holds, where $\tau_1 \in (0, 1)$. Furthermore, assume the contexts are generated through low-rank covariance structure (Case I ...) with $\varepsilon = \Theta(T^{-\tau_2})$, where $\tau_2 \in (0, \tau_1 / 4)$. Then, with $\overline{\tau} = \min\cbr{{\tau_1}/  {2}, \tau_2, \tau_1 - 4\tau_2} > 0$, EtC with the exploration duration $T_0 = \Theta(Kd)$ is a no-regret algorithm, and the regret satisfies R(T) = \tilde{O}(T^{\max\{\tau_1, 1 - \overline{\tau}/2\}}).

results.notes: Regret defined via expectations of f (pseudo-regret) against per-round optimal arm. EtC does not use T itself; marked anytime, but bound is along a sequence of instances with d tied to T.

symbols.tau_2: exponent with epsilon = Theta(T^-tau_2), tau_2 in (0, tau_1/2)

conditions: ||X_1^(i)|| = o(d^-c) and gamma_d^(i) >= c_underline Tr(Sigma)/d for sufficiently large d, some c > 0
low-rank covariance (Case I) with epsilon = Theta(T^-tau_2), tau_2 in (0, tau_1/2)

source.label: thm:etc_reg_simple_rbf
source.quote: Consider a kernel from the RBF class ... Suppose that $d = \Theta(T^{\tau_1})$ and Assumption~\ref{asmp:basic} holds ... Also, suppose that $\|X_1^{(i)}\| = o(d^{-c})$ and $\gamma_d^{(i)} \geq \underline{c} \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma_d^{(i)})/d$ ... Case I ... with $\varepsilon = \Theta(T^{-\tau_2})$, where $\tau_2 \in (0, \tau_1 / 2)$. Then, with $\overline{\tau} = \min\cbr{{\tau_1}/{2}, \tau_2, \tau_1 - 2\tau_2} > 0$, EtC with the exploration duration $T_0 = \Theta(Kd)$ is a no-regret algorithm, and the regret satisfies R(T) = \tilde{O}(T^{\max\{\tau_1, 1-2\tau_1, 1- c\tau_1, 1 - \overline{\tau}/2\}}).

symbols.Delta_len: lenient tolerance: per-round regret up to Delta_len is not counted

conditions: lenient regret R_Delta(T) = sum_t max{r(t) - Delta_len, 0} with fixed constant Delta_len > 0
setup of Theorem 4.6 with covariance Case I, II or III of Example 1
epsilon sufficiently small as a function of Delta_len (e.g. 3B^2 h''_max eps^2/4 + B^2 beta eps < Delta_len/(4K) in Case I)
tuning: T_0 = O(d), e.g. T_0 = ceil(256 sigma^2 K^2 eps / Delta_len) d (Cases I, II), T_0 = floor(eps^2 h''_min Delta_len/(64 sigma^2 beta)) d (Case III)

source.label: thm:etc_lr_Td
source.quote: Fix any $\Delta > 0$ as a constant. Consider the setup of Theorem \ref{thm:inner-product} with the cases I, II, and III ... assume that $d = \Theta(T^{\tau})$ holds for some $\tau \in (0, 1)$. Furthermore, each of the cases I, II, and III, if $\varepsilon$ is sufficiently small as a function of $\Delta$, then we can choose $T_0 = O(d)$ and the lenient regret for each of the three examples in Example \ref{ex:liang_sec4} is $R_{\Delta}(T) = O(d) = o(T)$.

results.notes: Quantity is lenient regret (Delta-tolerant pseudo-regret), recorded as 'other'. One record covers all three covariance cases.

symbols.tau: exponent with d = Theta(T^tau), tau in (0,1)

conditions: epsilon > 0 constant with -5 B^2 h'_min eps < Delta_len/(4K), h'_min = min_{a in [0,2]} h'(a) < 0
covariance Case I, II or III of Example 1
tuning: Case I: T_0 = ceil(256 sigma^2 K^2 eps/Delta_len) d; Case II: T_0 = ceil(256 sigma^2 K^2/(Delta_len eps)) d; Case III: T_0 = floor(Delta_len eps c_underline/(32 h'_min sigma^2)) d

source.label: thm:etc_lr_Td_rbf
source.quote: Fix any $\Delta > 0$. Suppose that Assumption~\ref{asmp:basic} holds and $\varepsilon > 0$ is constant. Furthermore, assume that $d = \Theta(T^{\tau})$ holds for some $\tau \in (0, 1)$. Then, the lenient regret for each of the three examples in Example \ref{ex:liang_sec4} is $R_{\Delta}(T) = O(T^\tau)$ if $\varepsilon$ is small enough such that $-5B^2 h_{\mathrm{min}}' \varepsilon < \frac{\Delta}{4K}$ ...
